answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the lagoon check immediately, the nectar audit keeps the resolved set and the atlas replay publishes exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Copying the same citations across 273 aliases therefore pays the reading cost 273 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
